title: Present Perfect
subtitle: Parler de l'expérience, du changement et du temps non terminé

theory.text: Dans cette leçon, tu vas apprendre le Present Perfect (have/has + participe passé) pour parler d'expérience, de changement et de temps non terminé.
A. Formation : have/has + participe passé
Le participe passé des verbes réguliers = base + -ed (worked, finished). Beaucoup de verbes courants sont irréguliers : be→been, go→gone/been, see→seen, do→done, have→had, write→written.

head: Forme
Règle
Exemple
rows: I have worked here for two years.
She hasn't finished the report yet.
Have you ever been to Dakar?
Yes, I have. / No, I haven't.
Have you finished? — Yes, I have.

theory.text: B. Quand utiliser le Present Perfect

head: Usage
Exemple
Note
rows: Expérience de vie (pas de moment précis)
I have visited three African countries.
She has just arrived — she's at the gate now.
He has worked at this company for five years.
Ce qui n'est pas encore arrivé (yet)
They haven't received the visa yet.
The airline has cancelled all flights today.

theory.text: C. For vs Since

head: Mot
Usage
Exemple
rows: She has lived in Bamako for ten years.
since + un point précis (point de départ)
a week, two months, a long time, years
I have known him for a long time.
Monday, last year, January, I was a child
I have known him since we were children.

theory.text: D. Present Perfect vs Simple Past

head: Temps
Usage
Exemple
rows: I have visited Paris. (on ne sait pas quand)
She has worked here since January.

theory.text: E. Expressions de temps courantes

items.note: I have already sent the email.
Haven't you finished yet?
The plane has just landed.
Have you ever worked abroad? — No, I've never worked abroad.
So far, everything has gone well.
He has recently changed jobs.

quiz.q: Complète : She _____________ (live) in Bamako for ten years.
Complète : I _____________ (never / visit) Senegal.
Complète : _____________ you _____________ (finish) the report yet?
Complète : They _____________ (not / receive) their visa yet.
I ___ Paris in 2019.
quiz.x: Simple Past : moment précis et terminé (2019).

quiz.q: She ___ here since January; she still works here.
quiz.x: Present Perfect : la situation continue au présent.

quiz.q: We ___ that film last week.
quiz.x: Simple Past : moment précis (last week).

quiz.q: ___ you ever ___ abroad?
quiz.x: Avec ever, on utilise le Present Perfect.

quiz.q: Traduis : Elle a déjà fini son travail.
quiz.a: She has already finished her work.
accept: She has already finished her work

quiz.q: Traduis : Avez-vous déjà visité le Sénégal ?
Traduis : Il travaille dans cette entreprise depuis 2018.
quiz.a: He has worked at this company since 2018.
accept: He has worked at this company since 2018
He has worked in this company since 2018

quiz.q: Traduis : Nous n'avons pas encore reçu la réponse.
quiz.a: We haven't received the answer yet.
accept: We haven't received the answer yet
We have not received the answer yet

quiz.q: Traduis : Le vol vient d'atterrir.

title: Modal Verbs
subtitle: Exprimer la capacité, l'obligation, le conseil et la permission

theory.text: Dans cette leçon, tu vas apprendre les verbes modaux (can, could, must, have to, should, may, might) qui ajoutent du sens au verbe principal.
A. Capacité & possibilité

head: Modal
Usage
Exemple
rows: He could swim when he was five.
I haven't been able to contact him.
Flights can be delayed in the rainy season.

theory.text: B. Obligation & nécessité

head: Modal
Usage
Exemple
rows: You must show your passport at the gate.
Employees have to wear a uniform.
You don't have to pay; it's free.
You mustn't smoke in the airport.
We need to confirm the booking today.

theory.text: C. Conseil & suggestion

head: Modal
Usage
Exemple
rows: You should arrive two hours before the flight.
He ought to apologise to his colleague.
You had better hurry, the gate is closing.

theory.text: D. Permission & demandes polies

head: Modal
Usage
Exemple
rows: May I see your boarding pass, please?
Could you help me with this form?
Would you mind closing the window?

theory.text: E. Possibilité & certitude (déduction)

head: Modal
Usage
Exemple
rows: He isn't answering; he must be in a meeting.
That can't be her office; it's closed.
The flight might be delayed because of the weather.

quiz.q: Complète : You _____________ show your passport at the gate. (obligation)
Complète : Employees _____________ wear a uniform at this company. (règle extérieure)
Complète : You _____________ pay; the visit is free. (aucune obligation)
Complète : You _____________ smoke in the airport. (interdiction)
Complète : He isn't answering his phone; he _____________ be in a meeting. (quasi-certitude)
Complète : That _____________ be her office; the light is off. (déduction négative)
You ___ show your ID; it's compulsory.
quiz.x: Obligation : must.

quiz.q: You ___ take an umbrella; it probably won't rain.
quiz.x: Aucune obligation : don't have to.

quiz.q: She ___ speak three languages.
quiz.x: Capacité : can.

quiz.q: That ___ be true — I saw it myself yesterday!
quiz.x: Quasi-certitude positive : must.

quiz.q: Traduis : Vous devez montrer votre passeport.
accept: You have to show your passport

quiz.q: Traduis : Il ne faut pas fumer ici.
Traduis : Pourriez-vous m'aider avec ce formulaire ?
quiz.a: Could you help me with this form?
accept: Could you help me with this form
Could you help me with this form please

quiz.q: Traduis : Ça ne peut pas être vrai.

title: Comparative & Superlative Adjectives
subtitle: Comparer les personnes, les lieux et les choses

theory.text: Dans cette leçon, tu vas apprendre à comparer avec le comparatif et le superlatif : more, the most, as...as.
A. Adjectifs courts (une syllabe, ou deux en -y)

head: Règle
Exemple
Note
rows: Bamako is bigger than Ségou. / Bamako is the biggest city in Mali.
This flight is nicer than the last one.
Dakar is busier than Ségou. / the busiest airport

theory.text: B. Adjectifs longs (deux syllabes ou plus)

head: Règle
Exemple
Note
rows: This job is more difficult than my last one.
This is the most interesting country I have visited.
This contract is less complicated than the other one.

theory.text: C. Formes irrégulières

head: Forme
Exemple
Note
rows: Her English is better than mine. / She is the best in the class.
Traffic is worse in the morning. / the worst traffic jam
The airport is farther than the train station.
He has less experience than she does.
She earns more money than before.

theory.text: D. Exprimer l'égalité et l'inégalité

head: Règle
Exemple
Note
rows: This flight is as expensive as the other one.
Mali is not as big as Algeria.
His salary is the same as mine.
This contract is different from the last one.

theory.text: E. Renforcer ou atténuer la comparaison

head: Règle
Exemple
Note
rows: This job is much better than the last one.
This flight is a bit more expensive.
She is by far the best candidate.

quiz.q: Complète : Bamako is _____________ (big) than Ségou.
Complète : This is the _____________ (interesting) country I have ever visited.
Complète : Her English is _____________ (good) than mine.
Complète : This job is _____________ (difficult) than my last one.
Complète : He has _____________ (little) experience than she does.
This suitcase is ___ than mine.
quiz.x: Adjectif court : heavy → heavier.

quiz.q: This is ___ interesting job I've ever had.
quiz.x: Superlatif d'un adjectif long : the most.

quiz.q: He is ___ far the best employee.
quiz.x: by far the + superlatif : de loin le meilleur.

quiz.q: That was ___ mistake of all.
quiz.x: bad → worse → the worst.

quiz.q: Traduis : Cette ville est plus grande que la mienne.
quiz.a: This city is bigger than mine.
accept: This city is bigger than mine
This city is larger than mine

quiz.q: Traduis : C'est le travail le plus intéressant que j'aie jamais eu.
quiz.a: It's the most interesting job I have ever had.
accept: It's the most interesting job I have ever had
It is the most interesting job I have ever had

quiz.q: Traduis : Son anglais est meilleur que le mien.
quiz.a: Her English is better than mine.
accept: Her English is better than mine
His English is better than mine

quiz.q: Traduis : Ce vol est aussi cher que l'autre.
quiz.a: This flight is as expensive as the other one.
accept: This flight is as expensive as the other one
This flight is as expensive as the other

quiz.q: Traduis : La circulation est pire le matin.
quiz.a: Traffic is worse in the morning.
accept: Traffic is worse in the morning
The traffic is worse in the morning

title: Singular & Plural Nouns
subtitle: Les pluriels réguliers et irréguliers, dénombrables et indénombrables

theory.text: Dans cette leçon, tu vas apprendre les pluriels réguliers et irréguliers, et la différence entre noms dénombrables et indénombrables.
A. Pluriels réguliers

head: Règle
Exemple
Note
rows: one bus → two buses; one box → two boxes
fin en consonne + -y : y → i, ajouter -es
one country → two countries; one company → two companies
one shelf → two shelves; one wife → two wives
one photo → two photos; one potato → two potatoes

theory.text: B. Pluriels irréguliers
C. Même forme au singulier et au pluriel

items.note: one sheep / twenty sheep
one fish / many fish
one series / two series
one aircraft / several aircraft

theory.text: D. Dénombrables vs indénombrables

head: Type
Règle
Exemple
rows: peut être compté, a un pluriel
pas de pluriel, use some/much/a lot of
luggage, information, advice, furniture, money, traffic
a piece of / a bit of + indénombrable
a piece of advice, a piece of information, a piece of luggage
how many + dénombrable / how much + indénombrable
How many bags do you have? / How much luggage do you have?

theory.text: E. Noms toujours au pluriel

items.note: I need to buy new clothes.
These trousers are too big for me.
Where are my glasses?
The police are investigating the theft.

quiz.q: Complète : One passenger, two _____________.
Complète : One child, three _____________.
Complète : One tooth, two _____________.
Complète : One box, two _____________.
Complète : One man, three _____________.
Complète : One company, two _____________.
Complète : How _____________ luggage do you have? (much / many)
Complète : How _____________ suitcases do you have? (much / many)
I need ___ advice before I sign the contract.
quiz.x: advice est indénombrable : a piece of advice.

quiz.q: There are ten ___ waiting at the gate.
quiz.x: person → people (pluriel irrégulier).

quiz.q: The police ___ investigating the theft.
quiz.x: police s'accorde toujours au pluriel.

quiz.q: Traduis : J'ai besoin d'informations sur le vol.
quiz.a: I need some information about the flight.
accept: I need some information about the flight
I need information about the flight

quiz.q: Traduis : Combien de bagages avez-vous ?
quiz.a: How much luggage do you have?
accept: How much luggage do you have
How much baggage do you have

quiz.q: Traduis : Combien de valises as-tu ?
quiz.a: How many suitcases do you have?
accept: How many suitcases do you have
How many bags do you have

title: Adjectives, Adverbs & Binomials
subtitle: Décrire précisément et utiliser des paires de mots figées

theory.text: Dans cette leçon, tu vas apprendre l'ordre des adjectifs, la formation des adverbes, les mots d'appréciation (+ gérondif/infinitif) et les expressions binomiales.
A. Ordre des adjectifs

head: Règle
Exemple
Note
rows: Opinion → Taille → Âge → Forme → Couleur → Origine → Matière + nom
a beautiful, small, old, round, black, Malian wooden box
an interesting job (not a job interesting)

theory.text: B. Former des adverbes à partir d'adjectifs

head: Règle
Exemple
Note
rows: même forme adjectif/adverbe : fast, hard, late
He works hard. (not hardly = presque pas)

theory.text: C. Mots d'appréciation + gérondif ou infinitif

head: Règle
Exemple
Note
rows: I prefer travelling by train to flying.
want / would like / hope + to + verbe
I would like to improve my English.
He can't stand waiting at the airport.

theory.text: D. Binomiales (paires de mots figées)

items.note: He kept walking back and forth in the hall.
Sooner or later, she will find a new job.
A good marriage needs give and take.
Add a little salt and pepper to taste.

items.en: now and then / now and again
items.note: We still meet up now and then.
The report is more or less finished.
There were papers here and there on his desk.
Every career has its ups and downs.
They arrived safe and sound.
By and large, the trip went very well.

quiz.q: Complète : She answered the question _____________ (quick).
Complète : He is a _____________, _____________ man. (opinion, âge : old / kind)
Complète : This is a _____________ box. (small, wooden, black — bon ordre)
Complète : She speaks English very _____________ (good).
Complète : He works very _____________ (hard) every day.
Complète : They arrived safe and _____________.
Complète : Every career has its ups and _____________.
She did the test ___.
quiz.x: On utilise l'adverbe : carefully.

quiz.q: He speaks very ___ English.
quiz.x: good qualifie le nom English (adjectif).

quiz.q: I prefer reading ___ watching TV.
quiz.x: prefer + -ing + to + -ing.

quiz.q: She enjoys ___ new people.
quiz.x: enjoy + -ing.

quiz.q: Traduis : Elle parle très bien l'anglais.
Traduis : Je préfère voyager en train plutôt qu'en avion.
quiz.a: I prefer travelling by train to flying.
accept: I prefer travelling by train to flying
I prefer traveling by train to flying

quiz.q: Traduis : Tôt ou tard, elle trouvera un nouvel emploi.
quiz.a: Sooner or later, she will find a new job.
accept: Sooner or later, she will find a new job
Sooner or later she will find a new job

title: Question Tags
subtitle: Les petites questions de fin de phrase

theory.text: Dans cette leçon, tu vas apprendre les question tags, ces courtes questions ajoutées à la fin d'une phrase : isn't it? don't you? shall we?
A. La règle de base

head: Règle
Exemple
Note
rows: You are from Mali, aren't you?
She doesn't work here, does she?
Le tag reprend l'auxiliaire/modal de la phrase
He works in Bamako, doesn't he?

theory.text: B. Tags avec les verbes modaux

head: Modal
Exemple
Note
rows: You can speak French, can't you?
We should leave now, shouldn't we?
You must renew your visa, mustn't you?

theory.text: C. Cas particuliers

head: Règle
Exemple
Note
rows: Let's book the flight now, shall we?

theory.text: D. Pourquoi utiliser les question tags

head: Usage
Exemple
Note
rows: You work at the bank, don't you?
You haven't seen my passport, have you?

quiz.q: Complète : You are from Mali, _____________ ?
Complète : She doesn't work here, _____________ ?
Complète : They have arrived, _____________ ?
Complète : He works in Bamako, _____________ ?
Complète : You can speak French, _____________ ?
Complète : I'm late, _____________ ?
Complète : Let's book the flight now, _____________ ?
Complète : There's a problem, _____________ ?
You work at the bank, ___?
quiz.x: Phrase affirmative → tag négatif.

quiz.q: She can't drive, ___?
quiz.x: Phrase négative → tag positif.

quiz.q: Let's go, ___?
quiz.x: Avec let's, on utilise shall we.

quiz.q: Traduis : Vous venez du Mali, n'est-ce pas ?
accept: You are from Mali, aren't you

quiz.q: Traduis : Il ne travaille pas ici, n'est-ce pas ?
quiz.a: He doesn't work here, does he?
accept: He doesn't work here, does he
He does not work here, does he

quiz.q: Traduis : Elle peut parler anglais, n'est-ce pas ?
quiz.a: She can speak English, can't she?
accept: She can speak English, can't she
She can speak English, can she

title: Airports & Air Travel
subtitle: Enregistrement, sécurité, embarquement et arrivée à l'aéroport

theory.text: Dans cette leçon, tu vas apprendre le vocabulaire de l'aéroport et du voyage en avion : l'enregistrement, le passage de la sécurité, l'embarquement, l'immigration et l'arrivée.
A. Avant le vol — Enregistrement & sécurité

items.note: Please have your boarding pass ready before you go through security.
We arrived two hours early to find the check-in counter.
Economy passengers have a baggage allowance of 23 kilos.
I only travel with carry-on luggage for short trips.
The security check took almost thirty minutes.
We had a coffee in the departure lounge.
Our boarding gate changed at the last minute.
Put your bag in the overhead compartment, please.
He had to pay extra for excess baggage.
She bought some perfume at the duty-free shop.
We have a three-hour layover in Casablanca.
I prefer a direct flight, even if it's more expensive.
I almost missed my connecting flight.

theory.text: B. Immigration, douanes & documents

items.note: There was a long queue at passport control.
You need a visa to travel to that country.
Fill in the customs declaration before landing.
The customs officer asked me to open my suitcase.
We walked through the nothing-to-declare lane.
He is waiting for his residence permit.
The two countries share a long border.
The immigration officer asked about the purpose of my visit.
An identity check is required before boarding.
Make sure your passport is still valid for six months.
My passport expired last month.
Business was the purpose of his visit.

theory.text: C. Dans l'avion

items.note: I always ask for an aisle seat so I can get up easily.
My daughter loves the window seat.
Please fasten your seatbelt.
The flight attendant brought us some water.
We had some turbulence over the ocean.
Keep your seatbelt on during take-off.
The landing was very smooth.
The cabin crew checked everyone's seatbelt.
Do not block the emergency exit.
Please put your tray table up.
The in-flight meal was surprisingly good.
It took me two days to recover from jet lag.

theory.text: D. Arrivée & problèmes

items.fr: la zone de récupération des bagages
items.note: Our suitcases were already at baggage claim.
We had to report our lost luggage.
Our flight was delayed by two hours.
The airline cancelled our flight because of the storm.
He missed his flight because of traffic.
Passengers can ask for compensation for long delays.
The airline offered a full refund.
The agent rebooked us on the next flight.
Our flight leaves from Terminal 2.
He was waiting in the arrivals hall.
We took the shuttle bus to the car park.
Luckily, our flight was on time.

theory.text: « layover » et « stopover » désignent tous les deux « l'escale » ; « flight attendant » peut se traduire par « hôtesse de l'air » ou « steward ».

quiz.q: Associe chaque mot anglais à sa traduction française.
Associe chaque mot anglais à sa traduction française.
Quel mot signifie « la carte d'embarquement » ?
quiz.x: « boarding pass » = la carte d'embarquement.

quiz.q: Quel mot signifie « le contrôle de sécurité » ?
quiz.x: « security check » = le contrôle de sécurité.

quiz.q: Quel mot signifie « l'excédent de bagages » ?
quiz.x: « excess baggage » = l'excédent de bagages.

quiz.q: Quel mot signifie « l'escale » ?
quiz.x: « layover / stopover » = l'escale.

quiz.q: Quel mot signifie « le visa » ?
quiz.x: « visa » = le visa.

quiz.q: Quel mot signifie « le titre de séjour » ?
quiz.x: « residence permit » = le titre de séjour.

Complète : Put your bag in the ______, please.
Complète : I prefer a ______, even if it's more expensive.

title: Professions & Employment
subtitle: Métiers, contrats, embauche, salaire et avantages

theory.text: Dans cette leçon, tu vas apprendre le vocabulaire des métiers, des contrats de travail, de l'embauche, du départ d'un emploi, du salaire et des avantages.
A. Les métiers courants

items.note: She works as an accountant at a trading company.
My brother is a civil engineer.
We called an electrician to fix the wiring.
The mechanic checked the engine carefully.
He hired a lawyer to check the contract.
The nurse took my blood pressure.
Ask the pharmacist which medicine is best.
The architect showed us the plans for the house.
He works as a truck driver.
The tailor took my measurements for the suit.
She worked as a translator for a foreign company.
He has been a civil servant for ten years.
She's an entrepreneur in the fashion industry.
We hired a consultant to improve our sales.

theory.text: B. Statut & contrats de travail

items.note: After the trial period, she got a permanent contract.
His fixed-term contract ends in December.
The probation period is usually three months.
She is doing a six-month internship at a bank.
He works as a freelancer, not for one company.
My aunt is self-employed; she runs her own shop.
She has a full-time job at the hospital.
He works part-time while studying.
Our employer offers good training programmes.
All employees must attend the meeting.
My colleagues are very supportive.
Nurses often do shift work.
Remote work became common after the pandemic.

theory.text: C. Trouver, garder & perdre un emploi

items.note: I applied for a job at the bank.
The job interview lasted forty-five minutes.
The company hired three new engineers.
She was promoted to team leader.
He resigned after ten years at the company.
The factory laid off fifty workers.
She was fired for being late every day.
He has been unemployed for six months.
Unemployment is a big problem in many countries.
My father retired at sixty.
She has to work a one-month notice period.
He made a career change from teaching to IT.

theory.text: D. Salaire & avantages

items.note: Her salary increased after the promotion.
The minimum wage went up this year.
Check your payslip for any mistakes.
All staff received a bonus this year.
He did a lot of overtime last month.
She took two weeks of paid leave.
He is on sick leave this week.
She is on maternity leave until March.
He receives a small pension.
She asked her boss for a pay rise.
Tax deductions are shown on the payslip.

theory.text: « fire / dismiss » = licencier (pour faute), tandis que « lay off » = licencier (motif économique).

quiz.q: Associe chaque mot anglais à sa traduction française.
Associe chaque mot anglais à sa traduction française.
Quel mot signifie « le/la comptable » ?
quiz.x: « accountant » = le/la comptable.

quiz.q: Quel mot signifie « l'électricien(ne) » ?
quiz.x: « electrician » = l'électricien(ne).

quiz.q: Quel mot signifie « l'avocat(e) » ?

theory.text: Dans cette leçon, tu vas apprendre à parler de l'origine des gens, des continents et des langues qu'ils parlent.
A. Pays & nationalités

items.note: He is French; he comes from France.

items.note: Where are you from? — I'm from Mali.

theory.text: D. Les langues du monde

items.note: English is spoken as a first or second language almost everywhere.
French is the official language of Mali.

Mandarin Chinese has more native speakers than any other language.

title: A Trip to the Airport
subtitle: Le voyage en avion, pas à pas

theory.text: Lis cette histoire sur un premier voyage en avion, puis réponds aux questions. Elle utilise le vocabulaire de l'aéroport et la grammaire du niveau 3 (present perfect, modaux).
✈️ A Trip to the Airport

Aminata had never flown before, so she arrived at the airport three hours early. She checked in at the counter and received her boarding pass. A friendly employee weighed her suitcase and told her it was under the baggage allowance, which was a relief.

The security check was faster than she had expected. An officer checked her passport and asked a few questions about the purpose of her visit. Once she had passed through, she found the departure lounge and bought a bottle of water before heading to her boarding gate.

When she boarded the plane, a flight attendant showed her to a window seat. She fastened her seatbelt and watched the airport grow smaller during take-off. The flight was smoother than she had imagined, although there was a little turbulence over the sea.

After several hours, the plane began its descent and the landing was gentle. Aminata collected her luggage at baggage claim and walked through the nothing-to-declare lane. Outside the terminal, her cousin was waiting for her, holding a small sign with her name on it. "It was a long haul," she admitted, "but it has been worth it."
